patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hive and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Hive only if your buying job matches “Work management platform with free plan (≤10 members) and Teams from $12/user/mo annual — ” rather than Notion's shape. Choose Notion only if your buying job matches “Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo ann” rather than Hive's shape. Workflow advantage: Hive leans project-tracking; Notion leans shared coverage. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hive and Notion share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Hive is Work management platform with free plan (≤10 members) and Teams from $12/user/mo annual — strong monday.com peer.; Notion is Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/user/mo annual; AI on Business..
- Workflow coverage skew: Hive-leaning project-tracking vs Notion-leaning —.
- Researched limits: Hive — Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams; Notion — Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management.

Limitations — Hive: Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams; Free storage (200MB) and AI credits (1k) are tight for active teams; Notion: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management; Reporting/dashboards thinner than dedicated PM tools.

Poor-fit cases: Hive is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams · Notion is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a full Work OS for portfolio/resource management · Avoid Hive if you actually need Notion's motion (Docs-first workspace with databases and light project tracking — Plus from $10/u)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
